item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for new, wholesome-ish SCP
item.content:encoded: At the moment, it seems like you're trying to build a narrative around the dollhouse instead of using it in an overarching story, so I'm going to ask you a quick question: what kind of story do you want to tell here? I know that's a rather general ask, so please interpret it however you like.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for new, wholesome-ish SCP
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for taking a look! Response below.

+ show block
– hide block

I have no specific narrative planned at the moment. What I have is just beats I wanted to hit and concepts to play with: the "Home Sweet Home" sign and the out-of-place doll suggests a potential story about someone without a home finding one in the doll house.

I imagine a D-Class or researcher who never really knew her/his/their family possessing the doll and not wanting to leave the house, the narrative borne out chiefly through radio communication logs (perhaps through a toy walkie-talkie placed in the house that then turns into a high-quality two-way radio from the subject possessing the doll's perspective) and/or journal entries. Perhaps the D-Class's description of the place and how nice it is makes a researcher jealous and they end up switching places with them without permission? Though I don't know how they'd think they'd get away with that for long…

Then maybe the research team purposely switches to a test subject that had a happier home life or whose psychological profile suggests they'd get bored or feel trapped. They reason that test subject would eventually want to leave and explore outside the house…

Perhaps, actually, it would be best to get rid of the possibility of switching out test subjects, and just have enough evidence discovered beforehand for them to know the best way to set up an experiment. The person that goes in is stuck there until they die walking through the portal. This could lay the narrative on a single character, and prevent the research team from simply changing test subjects before they get too comfortable inside…

Sorry, I guess this turned into more brainstorming than anything. I know I haven't given a lot of specifics, but does any of this feel like a step in the right direction or have I still not provided enough to work with? (I imagine the latter. Sorry if I'm wasting your time.)

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for new, wholesome-ish SCP
item.content:encoded:
Placeholder! Got summoned via PM to take a look-see. Will crit in a bit.

Alright, here’s my take.

+ show block
– hide block

I do think your core anomaly has potential here. While visitable dollhouses aren’t an uncommon concept in fiction (see Joe Hill’s recent horror comic The Dollhouse Family for a particularly excellent example), your choice to avoid any malevolence could allow for a novel narrative.

With that being said, I’m not seeing any sort of narrative at the moment. Modern SCP articles tend to use their respective anomalies as a jumping-off point to tell stories within the confines of the clinical document. By describing the dollhouse and its effects, you’re effectively presented us with a setting (the house) and characters (the dolls) without doing anything else with them. What do you plan to use to fill the space between the beginning of the article and its end?


If you respond to this comment and would like me to see it, please send me a Wikidot PM, as I will not be notified otherwise.

item.title: Seeking greenlight for new, wholesome-ish SCP
item.content:encoded:
It's a doll-house replica of the abandoned house it is found in. Entering the room with the doll house causes you to enter the body of an out-of-place doll in the doll house…

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: It's a doll-house replica of the abandoned house it is found in. Entering the room with the doll house causes you to enter the body of an out-of-place doll in the doll house.

Central Narrative: The room is an old craft room. There are handmade dolls, but none of them look like the one subjects inhabit when they enter, which looks like a mass-manufactured doll. On the table the doll house sits on is a sign that says "Home Sweet Home", with a matching one on the wall of the doll's kitchen.

The bodies of subjects who enter the room through the door go limp and collapse to the floor (like a doll LOLOLOL), having fallen into a coma. Subjects awaken within the doll in the house. From inside, the house seems like a real house – the abandoned house, in fact, but in its heyday. It is populated by a family (the other dolls), who are warm and inviting. Subjects feel like they could live there forever (not anomalously so, but it would be a comfortable life). Those observing the doll house from the outside can see the dolls moving about as though manipulated by a child.

+ show block
– hide block

The only way a subject can stop possessing the doll is if another person enters the room through the door, whereupon they switch places; the first subject awakens from their coma and the other collapses.

Subjects trying to leave the doll house through the front or back door are met with gentle resistance from the other dolls. With enough insistence, the dolls will sadly allow the subject to walk out. Exiting puts them in a dark, hellish landscape topologically matching the abandoned home. The front door of the real-world home appears to them as a huge glowing portal. Upon walking through it, they disappear and the comatose body dies. Another completely different doll then immediately materializes in the doll house, inert.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This morphed from horror into something more wholesome in the process of conceiving it and honestly I think that became its strong suit.

Additional Notes: My knowledge of the catalog is far from comprehensive, so my main worry is that something that hits similar beats has already been done.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
